prompt.context: Our client is the president of Zippy Snowmobiles. It makes snowmobiles for recreational users only. Zippy has faced falling sales over the past 7 years, of 7% per year, or about 40% over that period. Zippy's president has hired McKinsey to investigate and reverse this trend.
prompt.question: What areas would you like to explore to investigate and reverse Zippy's falling sales trend?

clarifying_info.q: What is the overall market trend?
clarifying_info.a: The overall market has also declined roughly 40% over the same 7-year period.
Key competitors include Northpoint, Gemco, and Sierra — details visible in Exhibit 1.

clarifying_info.q: What is the expected market size change for 2009 vs 2008?
clarifying_info.a: The overall market is expected to decline 8% from 2008 to 2009.

clarifying_info.q: What is the retail price of each snowmobile?
What is the variable cost of producing each snowmobile?

exhibits.title: Snowmobile Market Revenue by Competitor (2002–2008)
exhibits.shows: A table or chart of annual revenue figures for Zippy and its competitors (Northpoint, Gemco, Sierra) from 2002 to 2008, showing how each player's revenue has changed over the 7-year period.
exhibits.data: Total market 2002: $190M; Zippy 2002 revenue: $75M (~40% share); Northpoint disappears from the market; Gemco revenue spurt after Northpoint exit; Sierra market share increases despite overall market decline.

exhibits.title: Number of Zippy Snowmobiles Sold in One Year
exhibits.shows: A breakdown of the number of Zippy snowmobiles sold in a single year, segmented to show current sales volume and an incremental increase from a proposed marketing promotion.
exhibits.data: Current year sales: 1,000 units; projected incremental units from gas-card promotion: 100 additional units; total with promotion: 1,100 units.

framework: Market: Assess overall market size, growth trajectory, competitive landscape, and criteria for success
Revenue: Analyze pricing power, sales volumes, product mix, and seasonal balance
Costs: Ensure proposed revenue solutions do not create diseconomies of scale or harm profitability
Risks: Stress-test any sales improvement proposal for potential risks and implementation barriers

questions.prompt: Phase 1 — Market analysis: Using Exhibit 1, what does the competitive landscape tell you about Zippy's situation?
questions.guidance: Strong answer covers three points: (1) The overall market has shrunk ~40% over 7 years — Zippy's problem reflects an industry-wide decline, not just Zippy-specific issues. (2) Northpoint has disappeared from the market — possibly acquired by Gemco, which saw a revenue spurt afterward; study Northpoint's demise for cautionary lessons. (3) Sierra's market share has actually increased in the declining market — Sierra's strategies may offer best-practice clues.

questions.prompt: Phase 2 — Revenue growth strategies: What organic and inorganic strategies could Zippy pursue to grow revenue?
questions.guidance: Strong answer references the Ansoff Matrix and covers: M&A with other players (e.g., acquire Sierra); organic market penetration; bundling/tying/loss-leader pricing to maximize revenue per sale; extending the product line for seasonal balance (complementary products that sell in summer); extending to new geographic markets (overseas, more regions); segmentation to find underserved customer groups (children, physically challenged users) as a blue-ocean play.

questions.prompt: Phase 3 — Market share math: What increase in market share does Zippy need in 2009 vs. 2002 to maintain the same revenue dollars as in 2002? (The overall market is expected to decline 8% from 2008 to 2009.)
questions.guidance: Walk through the following steps clearly: identify 2002 revenue and market share, project 2009 total market, then back-solve for required share. Note that 2008 total market is $120M (derived from 2002's $190M declining ~40%).

math.setup: Zippy 2002 revenue = $75M; Total market 2002 = $190M → Zippy 2002 share ≈ 40%. Total market 2008 ≈ $120M (after ~40% decline). Total market 2009 = (1 − 8%) × $120M. Required 2009 share = $75M ÷ 2009 market.
steps: Increase in market share = 70% − 40% = 30 percentage points (or ~75% relative increase)
math.answer: Zippy needs approximately 70% market share in 2009, a ~30 percentage-point increase over its 2002 share of 40%.

questions.prompt: Phase 4 — Promotion profitability: Using Exhibit 2, evaluate the incremental profits from the CMO's gas-card promotion. Each buyer receives a $200 gas card; expected redemption rate is 30%; Zippy bears the full cost of redeemed gas.
questions.guidance: Set up an incremental profit formula: Additional units × contribution margin − cost of redeemed gas cards. Ensure the candidate uses only the 100 incremental units (not 1,100) for the revenue uplift, but applies the gas-card cost to all 1,100 cards issued.

math.setup: Incremental profit = Additional customers × (Price − VC) − (Redemption rate × Gas card value × Total cards issued). Additional customers = 100; Price = $50,000; VC = $20,000; Redemption rate = 30%; Gas card value = $200; Total cards = 1,100.
math.answer: The gas-card promotion generates approximately $2.93M in incremental profit.

brainstorming.prompt: What revenue growth strategies could Zippy pursue to reverse its sales decline?

categories.name: M&A / Inorganic Growth
ideas: Acquire Sierra (growing share in declining market; best-practice source)
Study and learn from Northpoint's failure

categories.name: Organic Growth — Market Penetration
ideas: Bundling accessories or financing to increase revenue per sale

categories.name: Organic Growth — Product Extension
ideas: Develop complementary summer products (ATVs, watercraft) to improve seasonal balance
Create children's or entry-level snowmobile segment
Develop accessories and aftermarket parts revenue

categories.name: Organic Growth — Market Extension
ideas: Expand to new geographic regions domestically
Enter international markets (e.g., Canada, Scandinavia, Russia)
Target underserved segments: physically challenged users, guided tour operators

categories.name: Pricing and Revenue Optimization
ideas: Introduce tiered product line (entry / mid / premium)
Use tying strategies (sell snowmobile at margin; profit on consumables/service)

recommendation: Zippy's falling revenues mirror a broad industry-wide decline of ~40% over 7 years — the problem is structural, not solely internal

Reversing the trend requires a two-pronged approach: organic growth measures (seasonal product extension, new geographies, targeted promotions such as the gas-card plan generating ~$2.93M in incremental profit) and strategic M&A (Sierra is a strong candidate given its growing share)
risks: M&A integration risk and valuation risk if acquiring Sierra or Gemco
Organic growth may be insufficient to offset continued market contraction
Gas-card and similar promotions compress margins if redemption rates exceed projections
New market entry (international) requires local regulatory and distribution knowledge
next_steps: Conduct due diligence and valuation on Sierra as a potential acquisition target
Model full-year impact of gas-card promotion and consider scaling if ROI holds
Assess feasibility of complementary summer-product line to reduce seasonality
Benchmark Sierra's practices to identify transferable best practices for Zippy
